=== Protest Letter to PUC.docx ===
Date: July 7, 2026
Public Utility Commission of Texas
William B Travis Building
1701 N. Congress Ave Suite 7-110
Austin, TX  78701

RE: Protest letter against Oncor & LCRA TSC  Bell County East to Big Hill 765KV Transmission Project (Docket 59475)
Dear Chairman Gleeson and Commissioners,
Thank you for your service to our state and for your continued commitment to protecting Texas Communities from irresponsible infrastructure projects.  I am writing today to express my Protest against the Bell County East to Big Hill 765KV Transmission project proposed by Oncor and LCRA TSC.
As a resident of the area, I can confirm that this project does not fit our community values.  Our area has intentionally pursued measured, deliberate growth, prioritizing rural character, land stewardship and community over rapid or infrastructure-driven expansion.  And while bringing no benefit to our area it also poses serious risks and I would like to highlight several specific concerns:
Burden of cost to Texas Ratepayers of the fully financed cost of the line.
Insufficient care giving proper notice to affected landowners to have full access to 30-day response time for Intervenor Application.  While my husband and I knew about the line we did not find out that we would be directly affected until we received our packet at the end of March 2026.  We had exactly 2 weeks to digest and get our pro se Intervenor ducks in a row.  For senior citizens who do not have a legal mind, we had to quickly find someone who could decipher the information that we were given and there was no way that we could get a lawyer to represent us in the hearing because it was far too late in the process.  I know that Oncor said that they did everything they had to do “legally” but when there were links that were added AFTER the paperwork was filed then I don’t believe that that constitutes transparency.  
Proximity to homes, parks, livestock land water wells, raising safety, health and quality of life concerns for families who have built their multigenerational lives here.
Destruction of historic ranches, archaeological sites and valuable cultural resources that help define the legacy of our region.
Economic impacts, decreased property values, decreased hunting revenues and increased cost from road degradation during construction. 
Environmental impact to habitat of all types and impact on karst limestone due to massive pilings under the unprecedented size of towers.
Safety concerns, increased wildfire risk and interaction with natural gas pipelines and inadequately prepared and economically strapped volunteer fire departments.
Given the magnitude of these concerns, and the overwhelming lack of public support, I respectfully request that you deny and CCN amendment applicant has for this project.  
Thank you for your time and consideration on this urgent matter, 
Sincerely,
Robert F. Pool & Lyn A. Pool
